answer: Each season a market opens at the summit pass at the sun's zenith, and every agent arrives with one basket woven from a willow coppice it tended below. The warden weighs the basket, counts its rods and matches the weave to the pattern cut into the agent's tally stick, then weighs it again at dusk, since green willow dries at a known rate and bought rods hold their weight. A basket failing either weighing loses its stall. A thousand fake agents need a thousand coppices tended all season, a thousand baskets woven, and a thousand climbs to the summit.
